items.title: Docs: contractor intake goes in the construction dashboard
items.body:
## Summary

A docs-only follow-up to Kghaffari26/sam-agent#3. The contractor intake form belongs in `Kghaffari26/construction-dashboard`, not agents-hub. This PR changes no code, because the recommender (`agents/grants/recommend.py`, `tools/setup_contractor.py`) doesn't depend on any particular dashboard.

- `CLAUDE.md`: adds `construction-dashboard` to the repo split. Contractors enter their details there, and that intake feeds `tools/setup_contractor.py`.
- `docs/specs/SPEC_GRANTS.md` §2.1: says the intake comes from the construction dashboard.
- `STATUS.md`: the intake form is listed as not done in construction-dashboard, which has no app code yet. agents-hub still only needs labels for the new reject codes.
- `DECISIONS.md`: records the owner's correction.

The branch includes one merge commit, which merges this branch's pre-squash tip so the push didn't need a force-push. The resulting tree is `main` plus these four doc files.

## Testing
- `uv run pytest`: 294 passed. Docs only.

items.title: Profile filters, scoring preferences and contractor setup
items.body:
## Summary

Adds three things to the grants agent:

### 1. `[filters]` in the business profile (SPEC §5.2a)
- **SAM.gov's own search filters:**
  - NAICS and PSC: exact codes or prefixes such as `5415`. Contracts only; a contract with no code listed passes.
  - Agency: matches agency, sub-agency or office.
  - Set-aside: `NONE` means unrestricted.
  - Keywords: any of / all of, over title + description.
  - Posted within N days, due within N days.
- **Filters the website doesn't have:**
  - Exclude sole-source set-asides and "intent to sole source / award" notices.
  - Check negative keywords against the description too.
  - Require a deadline, or a known value.
- **Applied locally**, after the SAM window fetch, which stays unfiltered. A server-side filter would leave a permanent gap in the fetched window whenever someone loosened it.
- **Output:** ten additive `stats.rejected` codes (SPEC §6.4). The schema snapshot is regenerated. agents-hub reads `stats.rejected` as `z.record`, so the current site accepts them and shows the raw codes until it adds labels.

### 2. `[scoring]` (SPEC §5.4a)
- Rubric weights (must sum to 100), a set-aside bonus, and Pursue/Consider bands for each profile.
- All applied in code. `refinalize` re-applies them to cached scores, so no LLM rescore is needed.
- The default weights equal the rubric ranges, so fit is exactly the old sum.
- `latest.json` `thresholds` publishes the bands actually in effect.

### 3. Contractor setup (SPEC §2.1)
- `agents/grants/recommend.py` turns a contractor's dashboard intake into a full profile with recommended filters and scoring, and a reason for each choice.
- It is rule-based over a catalog of 17 federal trades: no LLM, no network.
- `tools/setup_contractor.py` writes `config/profiles/<id>.toml` with the reasons as comments. Options: `--activate`, `--json` (for the dashboard), `--schema` (to build the intake form from).
- Examples: `config/intakes/*.json` → `config/profiles/*.toml`.

### Caching / cost
- `[filters]` and `[scoring]` are left out of `profile_hash` (`CODE_ONLY_SECTIONS`) because neither reaches a prompt.
- The live profile's hash is unchanged (`a872b5b…`, matches `data/grants/state.json`), so cached scores stay valid.
- No prompt changed, so no evals were run.

## Testing
- `uv run pytest`: 294 passed (245 before; all earlier tests unchanged).
- `ruff check .`: clean.
- No agent runs, no SAM requests, $0 spent.

## Follow-up (agents-hub)
- An intake form built from `setup_contractor --schema`.
- Labels for the new reject codes.

---

items.title: Next round: judge calibration and label review tooling, live research audit and fixes, email alerts
items.body:
Scope: `docs/specs/SCOPE_SAM_AGENT_NEXT.md` (S1–S4). S3 and S4 are done; S1 and S2 are built and wait on the owner's scores and label review.

## S3: live bid research audit and fixes
`scripts/audit_research.py` re-fetches every claim in the published briefs from USAspending.gov and SAM.gov. It runs as the new **Audit - Research** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`), because neither host is reachable from the dev container. Report: `docs/research_audit_2026-10.md`.

- Every concrete claim in the 5 live briefs matched its source: award ids, amounts, agency, NAICS, attachments and dollar figures.
- **Fixed at the cause**, each with a regression test built from the real response:
  - **Sub-agency sent as a toptier agency.** Navy, NOAA, FEMA and DHA were sent to USAspending as toptier agencies, which matched nothing, so 4 briefs said "no prior awards". They now go out as subtier filters (`usaspending.awarding_agency_filter`).
  - **Empty searches.** An empty search now falls back to the notice's agency and NAICS code without keywords.
  - **Keywords as one string.** A `keywords` string is now accepted instead of failing validation.
  - **Leaked tool-call markup.** Leaked `<parameter name=…>` markup in the `finish` call had emptied one brief's prior awards. The parameters are now repaired back into their fields, and the guard rejects any markup left in the text.
- Research prompt v1 → v2. Re-researched with the fixes, all 5 briefs pass every check and name the real incumbents. Research eval on v2: pass rate 1.00, every check 1.00 (including `required_tools`, which was 0.90), judge 0.95.
- The audit used 0 SAM.gov requests.

## S4: email alert digest
- `[alerts]` in `config/grants.toml` and `agents/grants/alerts.py` send one digest per run of strong new matches: fit ≥ 80, Pursue, at most 5 a day.
- Nothing repeats: what was sent is recorded by notice id + content hash in `data/grants/alerts.json`.
- Plain text plus simple HTML, sent through Resend.
- Sent by a new `alerts` job in `agent-grants.yml` after a successful run.
- Missing secrets or a delivery error never fail the run; the next run adds a `meta.warnings` line.
- `--dry-run` (and the workflow input `alerts_dry_run`) writes the digest to the job summary instead of sending it.

## S1 / S2: ready for the owner
- **S1:** `scripts/make_calibration_sheet.py` freezes 20 items (`evals/grants/calibration/`). Once they're scored by hand, `scripts/calibrate_judges.py` reports Spearman's ρ, MAE and a threshold mapping, and the suites take calibrated pass thresholds from `calibration.json`.
- **S2:** `scripts/review_labels.py` builds `labels_review.md` (the model's disagreements first, `r3-nsf-grant` at the top). `--apply` writes `labels_reviewed.json`, and the scoring suite switches to it.
- `scripts/import_review.py` brings in answers from the private review page.

## Checks
- 289 tests pass; ruff and actionlint are clean.
- Round spend $0.64 of the $3.00 cap.
- The Evals PR gate will re-run all three suites. Research v2's baseline is already in `evals/history.jsonl`.

## After merge (owner)
- Add the secrets `ALERT_EMAIL_API_KEY` and `ALERT_EMAIL_TO`.
- Run "Agent - Grants" by hand twice: the first run should send the digest, the second should send nothing new.

Gaps noted under "Needed from agents-core" in `STATUS.md`:
- extra secrets / a post-run hook in `run-agent.yml`
- Spearman and calibration history in evals
- repair of leaked tool-call parameters in `agent_loop`

items.title: SAM.gov request budget exhausted
items.body:
The SAM.gov search for 2026-10-07..2026-10-08 stopped at 1000 records on 2026-10-08: the daily budget (8 requests, `sam_daily_request_budget`) or SAM's rate limit ran out. The window catches up on the next runs; if this repeats, lower the lookback or use an entity-registered key (1,000 requests/day).

---
